rationale: 55/34 describes Hasan handing over a wallet and contains no shoulder-grasping. 55/35 has ṣədle b kaṯpe du ḥawro d Ḥasan and the corresponding German packte ... an der Schulter, in the same wallet story.

summary: File the refusal to take money under sense 2
rationale: lo+ṣədle kallawat means he did not take any money, as the supplied translation states. This is taking/keeping, sense 2 fassen, packen, behalten; sense 4 is showing honor/hospitality and requires that meaning, not merely a hospitable narrative context.

summary: File the hunting noun under Infinitiv
before: u=yawmo kule a=tre aḥunon-ani nəfqi-wa l-u=ṣaydo
after: u=yawmo kule a=tre aḥunon-ani nəfqi-wa l-u=ṣaydo
rationale: The cited 78/5 confirms nəfqiwa lu ṣaydo. The form belonging to ṣyd is the noun/infinitive ṣaydo after l-u=, to the hunt; nəfqi-wa is a past-tense form of nfq. There is no imperative of ṣyd in this example.

summary: Complete the shortened German perfect clause
rationale: The shortened quotation stops after erjagt, leaving that perfect clause without its auxiliary. The supplied edition continues erjagt und mir das Blut gebracht hast; retaining only the hunting clause requires its hast.
The comparative of schön is schönere; schonere is a spelling error.
In the idiom gloss to show respect/honor, hospitalit, the final y of hospitality is missing.
